{{nihongo|'''Uwato Shrine'''|宇波刀神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Kai Province]].

'''Uwato Shrine''' (うわとじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in Akeno-chō, {{ill|Hokuto, Yamanashi|Q825272|qid=Q825272}}, {{ill|Yamanashi Prefecture|Q132720|qid=Q132720}}. Its deities are {{ill|Takeminakata|lt=Takeminakata|Q9150391|qid=Q9150391|qid=Q9150391|lt=Takeminakata-no-Mikoto}}, {{ill|Izanagi|Q813858|qid=Q813858|lt=Izanagi-no-Mikoto}}, {{ill|Izanami|Q682306|qid=Q682306|lt=Izanami-no-Mikoto}}, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|abstract|Q272993|ar|سوسانو|azb|سوسانو|bcl|Susanoo|be|Сусанаа|bg|Сусаноо|ca|Susanoo|cs|Susanoo|da|Susa-no-o|de|Susanoo|el|Σουσάνoο|eo|Susanoo|es|Susanoo|eu|Susanoo|fa|سوسانو (خدا)|fi|Susanoo|fr|Susanoo|hr|Susano|hu|Szuszanoo|hy|Սուսանո|id|Susanoo|it|Susanoo|ja|スサノオ|ka|სუსანოო-ნო-მიკოტო|ko|스사노오|la|Susano'o|lb|Susanoo|mni|ꯁꯨꯁꯅꯨ-ꯅꯣ-ꯃꯤꯀꯣꯇꯣ|nl|Susanoo|pl|Susanoo|pt|Susanoo|ro|Susanoo|rsk|Сусано|ru|Сусаноо|simple|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|sl|Susanovo|sr|Сусаноо|su|Susanoo|sv|Susanoo|ta|சுசானவோ|th|ซูซาโนโอะ|tok|jan sewi Susano|tr|Susanoo|uk|Сусаноо|vi|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|zh|素戔嗚尊|zh_min_nan|Susanoo|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}}, and {{ill|Ukanomitama|de|Ukanomitama|eo|Ukanomitama|fr|Uka-no-Mitama|ja|ウカノミタマ|mni|ꯎꯀꯅꯣꯃꯤꯇꯃ|ru|Ука-но митама|simple|Ukanomitama|sv|Ukanomitama|th|อูกาโนมิตามะ|zh|宇迦之御魂神|qid=Q3080728|lt=Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto}}<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|和書 |title=Akeno Village History, main volume |edition=new edition |date=March 1996 |publisher=Akeno Village |pages=859,1267}}</ref>. Festival days are April 10 and October 5. The April grand annual festival date has been changed to the 2nd Sunday of April<ref>{{Cite book|和書 |title=Festivals and rites of Yamanashi - investigation report - |date=March 1999 |publisher=Yamanashi Prefectural Board of Education |page=125}}</ref>.

=== History ===
The founding era is unknown. However, a stone {{ill|Torii|Q234731|qid=Q234731}} bears inscription "{{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} 6 ({{ill|864|Q25041|qid=Q25041}})," and the shrine is treated as an Engishiki {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}, so it is inferred to have existed at least by the {{ill|Engi (era)|Q1374325|qid=Q1374325}} period ({{ill|901|Q23580|qid=Q23580}}-{{ill|923|Q30108|qid=Q30108}})<ref name="観光">[https://www.yamanashi-kankou.jp/rekitabi/jisha/spot/130.html Uwato Shrine] Yamanashi Tourism Organization "Travel Yamanashi history"</ref><ref name="散歩">Yamanashi Prefecture High School History/Civics Research Group (ed.), 'Historical Walk in Yamanashi' (Historical Walk 19), Yamakawa Shuppansha, 2007, pp.186-187</ref>.

It is also known that {{ill|Takeda Shingen|Q276404|qid=Q276404}} prayed here for victory during his Saku campaign ({{ill|Battle of Odaihara|Q1056249|qid=Q1056249}})<ref name="観光"/>.

The current haiden was rebuilt in April 1980, and the kaguraden was newly built<ref>{{Cite book|和書 |title=Yamanashi Prefecture Shrine Gazetteer |date=Sept 1985 |publisher=Yamanashi Shinto Youth Association |page=287}}</ref>.

This shrine has a stone torii. It is Myōjin-style and the only one of that form in former Akeno Village<ref name=":0" />. Its height is 2.52 {{ill|Metre|Q11573|qid=Q11573}}, but pillar diameter is as much as 43 {{ill|Centimetre|Q174728|qid=Q174728}}, giving a stout appearance. Built in the {{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}}, it is considered one of the oldest torii in Japan<ref name=":0" /><ref name="散歩"/>. Similar torii exists at {{ill|Katte Shrine|Q116979329|qid=Q116979329|lt=Katte Shrine}} in {{ill|Nirasaki, Yamanashi|Q290326|qid=Q290326}}, same prefecture.

=== Precinct ===
Within the precinct are the honden, haiden, kaguraden, watariden, and shamusho<ref name=":0" />.
